text: **dsh-carbon**（DSH 插件，Web 与 CLI）：估算 DeepSeek Harness 会话的碳排放。它从会话日志读取各模型的 token 用量，按带来源和置信等级的能耗因子计算 CO₂e，并在 Web 侧栏和命令行展示结果。主要功能包括按时间范围查看总量与区间、比较基础设施情景、查看会话和模型拆分、检查计算方法，以及导出分享卡片和徽章。适合希望了解 DSH 使用足迹并保留本地历史的用户。无需 API key；可选设置基础设施、DSH 主目录和历史文件位置。

**dsh-carbon** (DSH Web and CLI plugin) estimates session CO₂e from token usage and sourced energy factors. It shows confidence bands, date ranges, model breakdowns, methodology, and shareable cards. No API key is needed; local history and infrastructure settings are optional.

**dsh-carbon** 的功能「会话碳排估算」：按会话中各模型的输入、缓存和输出 token 用量，结合因子表计算 CO₂e，并给出低值、高值和因子置信等级。CLI 与 Web 报告均可查看。
**dsh-carbon** 的功能「历史会话汇总」：同步并保存每个会话的 token 记录，支持按日期范围汇总、查看模型及会话拆分；历史记录在原始会话日志不再存在时仍保留。
**dsh-carbon** 的功能「Web 碳足迹面板」：在 DSH 侧栏提供 Carbon 页面，显示时间线、排放估算、会话与模型摘要及方法说明；可切换统计区间和基础设施情景。
**dsh-carbon** 的功能「分享卡片与徽章」：通过 Web 路由或 CLI 输出包含排放估算的 SVG 卡片和徽章，卡片可下载，徽章可用于 README。
**dsh-carbon** 的功能「命令行报告」：运行 `dsh-carbon` 可查看汇总、可信区间、会话与模型拆分；还提供 timeline、sessions、json 和 methodology 等命令。
dsh-carbon 使用前须知：排放值是按模型因子推算的估算，并附有区间和置信等级；README 特别说明部分新模型没有公开能耗测量。
dsh-carbon 使用前须知：本地历史文件默认保存在 DSH 主目录下的 carbon/history.jsonl；首次同步前已经被清理的会话日志无法补回。

dsh-carbon README · dsh-carbon：Track the estimated carbon footprint of your [DeepSeek Harness](https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/en/guide/quickstart) sessions, in the terminal and in the web GUI.

dsh-carbon README · dsh-carbon：It takes the idea behind [claude-carbon](https://github.com/gwittebolle/claude-carbon), a local estimate built from token counts with a sourced methodology, and applies it to DeepSeek. The numbers are not ported. The published evidence for DeepSeek is much thinner, and borrowing Anthropic's factors would have produced a confident figure with nothing behind it.

dsh-carbon README · The web GUI：

The plugin adds a Carbon row to the sidebar and opens a page in the main panel.

dsh-carbon README · The web GUI：The page leads with a whale, and its colour is the reading: the same green to yellow to red ramp as the hero, on the same log scale, green up to 250 g and red from 5 kg. It blinks, and beats its fluke faster as the figure climbs. One character map in `lib/core/whale.mjs` draws it for the page and for the exported card, so the whale on your card is the one you saw on screen.

dsh-carbon README · The web GUI：Under it the estimate is never shown alone. There is a low/high band beside it and a marker showing where the point estimate sits inside that band. Below that, a row of stripes: one per day, week or month, coloured against the median period rather than a maximum, so a quiet week still reads as a stripe next to a busy one. Hovering or tabbing to a stripe names its date, total and session count. The toolbar switches the window between 7 days, 30, 90, 12 months and all time, remembered per browser, and shows the change against the previous window of the same length whenever there is one to compare.

dsh-carbon README · The web GUI：Then two bars split the same four kinds of token twice: how many there were, and what they cost in grams. Almost every token in a session is a cache read, and cache reads come to roughly a tenth of the grams. Output is half a percent of the tokens and nine tenths of the footprint. One bar would have hidden that.

dsh-carbon README · The web GUI：The rest is smaller. Equivalents in km driven, kettle boils and phone charges, from the same world-average factors the CLI uses. A switch between DeepSeek's own fleet and Azure that applies to every number on the page, totals, sessions, models, stripes and equivalents alike, and is remembered per browser. A Method tab with the formula, the deployment assumptions, each factor row with its tier, band, caveat and source, and the cross-checks underneath. English and Chinese, following the host locale, laid out for narrow main columns.

dsh-carbon README · The web GUI：Two buttons sit under the stripes. *Download card* renders the 1200×630 card as a PNG in the browser, with no native dependency, falling back to the SVG if the canvas refuses. *Copy badge* puts a shields.io markdown line on the clipboard. Both are described in [Sharing](#sharing).

The page refreshes every 30 seconds while it is visible, when the window regains focus, and on demand. The refresh button skips the host's 5-second cache.

dsh-carbon README · The web GUI：> **One restart for the first install.** The host caches whether a package has a `dsh.client` half for the lifetime of the process, so adding the browser half to an already-running harness needs one restart (or app relaunch) before **Carbon** appears in the sidebar, and again after the browser half's *declaration* changes. Rebuilding the bundle alone hot-reloads; a host-side change takes effect on the next recomposition.

dsh-carbon README · Install：Requirements: DeepSeek Harness **0.2.1-rc.3 or newer** (declared in `dsh.engines.dsh`), and Node **22.15+** only if you want the standalone CLI. The plugin itself runs inside the app.

**As a plugin.** The GUI is this half; the CLI comes with it.

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-carbon
```

dsh-carbon README · Install：That forwards to `pnpm add` inside the profile *and* appends the package to `dsh.profile.bundles`, so the only manual step left is restarting the harness once, which is when the browser half is discovered. If `dsh` is not on your `PATH`, it ships inside the app:

```bash
"/Applications/DeepSeek Harness.app/Contents/Resources/runtime/cli/bin/dsh" \
  plugin --profile desktop add dsh-carbon
```

dsh-carbon README · Install：After the restart the page lives in the sidebar as the Carbon row, between *Automation tasks* and *More*:

**`desktop` is a profile name, and it is whatever your install called it.** Check before you type it: ```bash ls ~/.dsh/profiles ```

dsh-carbon README · Install：A mistyped name is not an error. `--profile destkop` quietly creates a second, empty profile and installs the plugin into it, where the app will never look. If the Carbon row does not appear after a restart, check that first.

dsh-carbon README · Install：Without npm, the same tarball is attached to every [release](https://github.com/ValenscoA/dsh-carbon/releases), and `dsh plugin --profile desktop add <tarball URL>` accepts it too. By hand it is `pnpm add dsh-carbon` in the profile directory plus a `"dsh-carbon"` entry in `dsh.profile.bundles`.

**The CLI alone**, on Node 22.15 or newer:

```bash
npx dsh-carbon report
```

From a clone instead: `node bin/dsh-carbon.mjs report`.

dsh-carbon README · Commands：| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `dsh-carbon` | The report: totals, band, per-session and per-model, split by kind of token |
| `dsh-carbon timeline` | The stripes row in blocks, totals, the median period and the four kind shares |
| `dsh-carbon sync` | Bring the store up to date with the session logs |
| `dsh-carbon recompute` | Reprice every stored session from its token counts |
| `dsh-carbon card` | Write the shareable SVG card (`--out`, `--stdout`) |
| `dsh-carbon badge` | Print a shields.io badge for a README (`--svg`) |
| `dsh-carbon pr` | The repository's footprint since the branch point, posted to its pull request (`--dry-run`, `--pr N`) |
| `dsh-carbon sessions` | One line per session |
| `dsh-carbon json` | Machine-readable output |
| `dsh-carbon methodology` | Every factor, its source, its band and its caveats |

dsh-carbon README · Commands：Every reading takes `--range 7d|30d|90d|12mo|all`, `--since YYYY-MM-DD`, `--until YYYY-MM-DD` and `--infra china|azure|aws`. `report` also takes `--limit N`.

Environment: `DSH_CARBON_INFRA=azure` for the alternative-fleet reading, `DSH_HOME` to point at another harness home, `DSH_CARBON_HISTORY` to move the store.

dsh-carbon README · The store：Sessions live in `~/.dsh/carbon/history.jsonl`, one line each. The window, the stripes, the median and the change figure all come from that file.

Two decisions there are worth explaining.

dsh-carbon README · The store：**Rows store tokens, not grams.** Conversion happens on every read, using the factors in force at that moment, so correcting a factor re-prices the whole history with no migration step and no stale rows. `recompute` prints that total; it does not rewrite anything. What is stored is what was measured, meaning how many tokens of each kind crossed the wire. What is derived stays derived.

dsh-carbon README · The store：**JSONL rather than SQLite.** The file has to be readable and diffable by a person. The claim this tool makes is that you can check its arithmetic, and a database you need a shell to open works against that. A few thousand rows is a few hundred kilobytes, well below the point where the format matters.

dsh-carbon README · The store：Sync is incremental. Each row remembers the size and modification time of the log it came from, so an unchanged log is stat'd rather than parsed, and only a session that has grown is read again. When the harness prunes a transcript the row stays, which is the point of keeping the file at all, and the page reports how many of the total come from logs it can no longer check.
dsh-carbon README · Sharing：

dsh-carbon README · Sharing：`card.svg` is a 1200×630 card carrying the figure, its band, the fleet the factors assume, the stripes and the kind split, signed with the one sentence it should be signed with: *estimate, not a measurement*. It is rendered on the host as SVG, so the export path needs no browser, no native module and no network call. The page rasterises it in your browser when you ask for a PNG. `card --out` and `badge --svg` write the same files from the CLI.

dsh-carbon README · Sharing：`badge` prints a static shields.io markdown line whose message is the figure and the month it was taken. Static is deliberate. A live badge would publish your footprint to a third party every time someone loaded your README.

dsh-carbon README · Sharing：`pr` sums the stored sessions whose working directory sits inside the current repository, from the point the branch left the default branch, and posts one sticky comment through your own `gh` auth. It is weaker than `claude-carbon`'s attribution and says so. A branch is not recorded in a harness session log, so this is attribution by repository and time: it includes any session that ran in the same repository in that window, on any branch, and excludes work done before the branch point. `--dry-run` prints the comment and posts nothing.

dsh-carbon README · The honest part：`claude-carbon` can lean on measured per-token energy for the model family it tracks. This cannot, and the difference is worth stating plainly.

**What is measured.** Jegham et al. 2025 ([arXiv:2505.09598v6](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.09598)), Table 4, is the only public source of per-query inference energy covering DeepSeek. It measures **DeepSeek-V3** and **DeepSeek-R1** on DeepSeek's own Chinese datacenters and on Azure, at three prompt shapes.

dsh-carbon README · The honest part：**What is not.** It covers no V3.1, V3.2, V4, V4-Pro or Flash checkpoint. [EcoLogits](https://ecologits.ai) carries no DeepSeek model at all, so unlike `claude-carbon`'s Opus/Haiku rows there is no second **measurement** to bracket the extrapolations against. A Tier-3 cross-check is shown on the Method tab, but it is an estimate, not a bracket. The model this harness runs by default, **deepseek-v4.1-flash**, has **no published energy measurement whatsoever**.
dsh-carbon README · The honest part：**So the table is graded.** Every row carries a tier, and both the report and the GUI show the tier of whatever they used:

dsh-carbon README · The honest part：| Model | Tier | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `deepseek-v3` | **measured** | Fitted to the published per-query energies. Mean error 2.0%. |
| `deepseek-r1` | **measured** | Same source, but the fit is poor: mean error 30% (see below). |
| `deepseek-v4.1-flash` | **derived** | Scaled from V3 by active-parameter ratio, from the released `config.json`. |
| `deepseek-v4-pro` | **extrapolated** | No measurement and no released config. Widest band. |

dsh-carbon README · Deriving V4.1-Flash：V4.1-Flash has open weights, so its architecture is at least checkable. The released config gives 40 layers, 384 routed experts of intermediate width 2304, 6 active per token, 1 shared expert, plus MLA attention: about **14.2B active parameters** against V3's ~37B.

Both prefill FLOPs and decode bytes scale with active parameters, so both factors scale by the same ratio:

dsh-carbon README · Deriving V4.1-Flash：```
V4.1-Flash factor = V3 factor x (14.2B / 37B) = 0.38x
  input  28 g/Mtok -> 11 g/Mtok
  output 5289 g/Mtok -> 2028 g/Mtok
```

That is arithmetic from a released config. The assumption underneath it, that energy per active byte on DeepSeek's V4 serving stack matches V3's, is not verified. That is where the 0.5x-3.0x band comes from, and why the row is `derived` rather than `measured`.

dsh-carbon README · Why R1's factor is worse than V3's：Fitting `energy = a*input + b*output` to the three published R1 points gives a 30% mean error, against 2.0% for V3. The reason is diagnostic rather than cosmetic: R1 costs ~19 Wh even for a 100/300-token prompt. Most of its energy is **fixed per query** (long reasoning traces, prefill, scheduling) rather than proportional to tokens. A token-only model therefore under-reports short R1 sessions and over-reports long ones.
section: Why R1's factor is worse than V3's

text: dsh-carbon README · Why R1's factor is worse than V3's：`dsh-carbon` reports that error instead of hiding it. A per-query intercept term would fit better, but it needs a count of requests that the log does not cleanly provide, so the limitation is documented rather than papered over.
section: Why R1's factor is worse than V3's

text: dsh-carbon README · Why the input factor is the weak one：The three published points are close to collinear, so the input and output terms trade off almost freely. Unconstrained least squares puts the input coefficient **slightly negative** for the DeepSeek rows, which is obviously wrong and a sign that the data cannot separate prefill from decode. The derivation script therefore uses non-negative least squares and carries the input term across from the Azure fit, where it is positive and identifiable, rescaled to the China grid. It is a borrowed number, labelled as such.
section: Why the input factor is the weak one

text: dsh-carbon README · Deployment dominates：Jegham et al. measured the *same* DeepSeek-V3 at **13.162 Wh** on DeepSeek's own Chinese datacenters and **3.696 Wh** on Azure. A 3.6x gap from PUE, cooling and grid carbon intensity alone, wider than the gap between most model families.

dsh-carbon README · Deployment dominates：So the fleet assumption matters more than the model. The default is DeepSeek's own fleet, because DeepSeek Harness runs on DeepSeek's first-party API, and it is also the pessimistic reading. `DSH_CARBON_INFRA=azure` shows the optimistic one. The GUI's fleet switch does the same for a single page without touching the environment.

dsh-carbon README · Cross-checks：A second number is useful only if its limits travel with it. [Know Your Compute](https://www.knowyourcompute.com/models/deepseek-v4-flash) (July 2026) is a transparent Tier-3 calculator: for models without disclosures it estimates per-query energy from GPU power, model size and benchmark latency. Its DeepSeek-V4-Flash page gives **1.0 Wh and 0.53 g CO₂e per query** on a 525 gCO₂/kWh China grid.

dsh-carbon README · Cross-checks：Its V4-Pro figure (6.0 Wh) is six times its V4-Flash figure and sits at the top of this tool's 0.5-6x band: evidence that the point estimate may be low, not evidence that it is wrong. Its V3 page is the cautionary example instead. It says 2.0 Wh for a medium prompt, while the paper's China points are 2.777 / 8.864 / 13.162 Wh, and 2.0 Wh is close to the **Azure** medium point (2.165 Wh) paired with the China grid. That row is shown as `not used`.

dsh-carbon README · Cross-checks：The GUI's Method tab lists all three with their URLs and verdicts. None of them enters the arithmetic, and none changes a factor. A Tier-3 estimate cannot narrow a band whose width comes from physics nobody has measured.

dsh-carbon README · How it works：```
grams = ((input + cacheWrite) * inputFactor
       + cacheRead * inputFactor * 0.08
       + output * outputFactor) / 1e6
```

Cache reads are a prefill residual at 8% of the input factor. DeepSeek's 0.02 cache-hit *price* ratio is not an energy ratio and is deliberately not used.

dsh-carbon README · How it works：Token counts come from the session logs under `~/.dsh/sessions/*/*/session.v4.jsonl.zstd`, reading `data.usage` on `assistant/message` events and attributing each message to `data.message.source.model`, so a mid-session model switch is priced correctly. `inputTokens` already excludes cached tokens. `sync` folds those logs into the store (see [The store](#the-store)), and every reading is priced from the store rather than the logs, so a pruned transcript no longer loses its footprint.

dsh-carbon README · How it works：Assistant messages are deduplicated by `message.id`. A resumed or compacted session can replay messages that are already in the log, and counting a replay twice inflates the token sum with no symptom other than a larger footprint. `claude-carbon` found roughly 3x inflation from this. Across the logs read here no session had a repeat, so the count of ignored replays is reported rather than quietly absorbed.

dsh-carbon README · How it works：One implementation detail is worth knowing. The harness *appends* to these logs, one zstd frame per flush, and a live log had 168 frames. Node's `zstdDecompressSync` decodes only the first frame and silently returns a truncated log. This walks every frame, validating each candidate boundary by attempting the decode, and drops a half-written trailing frame, which Node decodes to a partial line rather than throwing. Without that, history would be silently under-reported by an order of magnitude.

dsh-carbon README · HTTP routes：The host plugin registers read-only routes, loopback-only and same-origin fenced. The GUI is a client of the same routes, so anything the page shows is available to a script.

dsh-carbon README · HTTP routes：| Route | Returns |
|---|---|
| `GET /dsh-carbon` | The window: totals, buckets, kind split, models, sessions |
| `GET /dsh-carbon/summary` | Same |
| `GET /dsh-carbon/timeline` | The same payload without the model and session rows |
| `GET /dsh-carbon/sessions` | Session rows only |
| `GET /dsh-carbon/methodology` | The full factor table with tiers, sources, equivalences and cross-checks |
| `GET /dsh-carbon/card.svg` | The shareable card (`?download=1` sets a filename) |
| `GET /dsh-carbon/badge.svg` | A shields-style badge of the all-time total |

dsh-carbon README · HTTP routes：All of them accept `?range=7d|30d|90d|12mo|all`, `?since=`, `?until=`, `?infra=azure|china|aws`, and `?fresh=1` to bypass the 5-second read cache. `/summary` and `/sessions` also take `?limit=N` (1 to 200 session rows, default 50). The payload carries `totals` (tokens by direction, calls, cost, measured/unmeasured), `buckets` (one per period, with its colour and load), `kinds` (tokens and grams per kind, with both shares), a `models` roll-up keyed by factor row, the world-average `equivalences`, and the session rows. Every gram figure is on the selected fleet, scaled exactly once.

dsh-carbon README · Development：```bash
npm test                 # 65 tests: factors, folding, store, windows, exports, client bundle
npm run build:client     # rebuild lib/client.js from src/client/
```

dsh-carbon README · Development：`lib/client.js` is committed and is the artifact the harness serves, so edit `src/client/` and rebuild rather than touching it. The bundle is built with esbuild, keeps React external against the shell's shared module table, and registers `dsh-carbon` on `window.__ModuleLoader__` in the format the client module system expects. The test suite loads that built bundle through a stubbed loader and renders the page with `react-dom/server`, so a broken bundle fails `npm test` rather than a user's sidebar.

dsh-carbon README · Tests：```bash
npm test                 # 65 tests; `npm install` first for the 9 browser tests
node --test test/*.test.mjs
```

dsh-carbon README · Tests：65 tests, including one that regenerates `lib/factors/factors.json` from `tools/derive-factors.mjs` and fails if the two have drifted, so the published numbers cannot silently diverge from their stated derivation. The report tests cover fleet scaling, the session-row cap, model roll-up and empty history. The client tests cover registration, both locales, the rendered rows, the method table, the heat scale's thresholds and hue direction, and the cross-check card. The store tests prove the two properties the design rests on: a session survives the deletion of its log, and an unchanged log is not parsed again. The export tests pin the invariant that matters most, that the buckets and the four kinds each sum to the window total, on every fleet.

dsh-carbon README · Artwork：The icon, the logo and the four banners come from the same sprite the page renders. `node scripts/make-art.mjs` writes the SVG, and `node scripts/make-png.mjs` renders each one to PNG in a headless Chrome at its own size. The whale in the banner is the whale in the app, so a change to the sprite moves every asset with it.

dsh-carbon README · Artwork：| File | Size | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `icon.svg` | 64×64 | the plugin's row in the harness |
| `docs/logo.png` | 512×512 | avatar slot, README badge |
| `docs/banner-horizontal.png` | 1280×640 | repository social preview, link cards |
| `docs/banner-square.png` | 1080×1080 | square posts |
| `docs/banner-vertical.png` | 1080×1350 | portrait posts |

dsh-carbon README · Publishing：Nothing in this package is tied to the author's machine: no absolute paths, no hard-coded home directory, no network call on any read path. The store is per-user at `~/.dsh/carbon/history.jsonl` (override with `DSH_CARBON_HISTORY`), and the plugin writes nothing else.

A plain `git clone && node --test test/*.test.mjs` runs the arithmetic without installing anything. The nine browser tests skip themselves with a note, because React is a devDependency and the shipped bundle never contains it.

dsh-carbon README · Publishing：A `npm pack` tarball installs cleanly into an empty project and produces a report against any `DSH_HOME`. The core test files also run from the installed package.

It ships by two routes carrying the same bytes: the npm package `dsh-carbon`, and a `.tgz` attached to each GitHub release for anyone who would rather not depend on the registry. `homepage` and `repository` are set, because the badge markdown and the page's *Copy badge* button link there.

Releasing a new version:

dsh-carbon README · Publishing：```bash
npm test                 # `prepublishOnly` runs it anyway
npm version patch        # or minor / major; commits and tags
git push --follow-tags
npm publish              # needs a granular token with "bypass 2FA"

dsh-carbon README · Publishing：The community registry at [awesome-dsh-plugin.com](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com) indexes GitHub repositories rather than receiving submissions, and lists a one-line `install` command per entry (`dsh plugin --profile web add <package>`). 3,823 of its 7,406 entries are npm packages. There was no carbon-footprint plugin in it when this was written.

dsh-carbon README · Limits：- **V4.1-Flash and V4-Pro figures are not measurements.** Treat them as an order of magnitude.
- **The store is only as old as its first sync.** Sessions the harness pruned before you installed this are gone, and nothing can rebuild them. From the first sync on, history survives pruning.
- **The band is judgement, not a confidence interval.** It has no statistical basis. It is the range the author would defend.
- **Costs use the peak tariff**, because a historical report cannot know which tariff applied. Off-peak is exactly half. The GUI's cost stat does not change with the fleet switch, since it is API pricing rather than electricity.
- **No per-request tracing.** One number per model per direction, like `claude-carbon`.
- **Cross-checks are estimates, not factors.** Know Your Compute's numbers appear on the Method tab for comparison and never enter the arithmetic. Its V3 row is explicitly rejected because it mixes an Azure energy reading with the China grid.
- **The GUI and the routes are read-only.** They read the store and never write to the profile. The only thing the plugin writes is its own `history.jsonl`.
dsh-carbon README · Licence：MIT. Factor values are derived from published research; see `lib/factors/factors.json` for per-row citations.
